# Independent review — head `9e8bdfc95c916b62550fb8c3142f804bbbfb2444` (base `cf19a52c…`)

**Verdict: source_clear_for_measurement** — no blocking correctness or resource-unsoundness defect found in the two-file change. Findings below are ranked; F1–F2 must be bounded by the next measurement, F3–F5 are pre-admission repairs, not measurement blockers.

## Soundness items I verified (not taken on claim)

- **Top-k cut**: the walk stops only at a *complete* object-id group (`exec.rs`, block-extension `while end < n && obj_id_at(end) == boundary_obj`), so every uncollected solution is strictly worse on the primary key than ≥ `row_budget` collected ones. Multi-valued probes outside the visited prefix therefore cannot displace collected rows even though they are never expanded. Correct.
- **Inline monotonicity**: `dict::try_inline_lit` admits only canonical `xsd:integer` in `0..=2^30-1` at `INLINE_BASE=2^31`, so ascending id = ascending value, and non-inline dictionary ids sort *below* `INLINE_BASE`, which makes `rows.iter().all(is_inline)` short-circuit on row 0 for string/negative/decimal predicates. The `all()` guard is O(1) in the common decline, O(n) only when the whole extent is admissible. Good.
- **Permutation assumptions**: seed `[None,Some(p),None]` sorted on col 2 resolves to `Pos` in both `BUILT` sets; probe `[None,Some(p),None]` needs `Pso` (absent under `compact-index`/wasm) and `[None,Some(p),Some(o)]` resolves to `Pos`. Both `actual_sort` checks are correct, and `subject_ids` is built *after* the check, so `partition_point` never runs on an unsorted slice. `subject_ids[start..]` at `start == len` is a legal empty slice.
- Shape guards are closed: repeated intra-triple vars, blank nodes, variable predicates, hub reuse, duplicated object vars, `order_var` bound by >1 pattern, residual FILTER, non-conjunctive, `unsat` (→ correct empty), `row_budget == 0`, `budget::active()`, `view::default_is_empty()`, `zk::enabled()`. `cols`/`out_to_cols` cannot desynchronise from `row_ids` because `emit` is unreachable on any `failed`/`match_count != 1` branch.
- Loop termination: `block_target.saturating_mul(4).max(visited_to + 1)` guarantees progress even when a group extension overshoots `block_target`; `clamp(visited_to, n)` never panics.

## F1 (measurement-gating, resource) — retained scans + per-probe `Vec<Id>` under an overlay

In the `other_pats` construction loop, each probe holds a live `Scan<'g>` **plus** a materialised `subject_ids: Vec<Id>` sized to that pattern's *global* extent, all simultaneously alive until return. Under a forked graph with pending deltas — the exact claim-queue workload this targets — `store::scan_with` takes `Cow::Owned(ov.merge(...))` for every one of the `k+1` scans, and `count_correction` iterates the whole tombstone set per scan. Peak is then ≈ `(k+1)` full range copies + `Σ 4·m_i`, versus the fallback's ~2 live scans, and on any decline (`min_other_card*2 < seed_card`, `max_group`, `match_count != 1`, `failure_budget`) that whole cost is paid *and then* the fallback runs. It is bounded by store size and `budget::active()` is false by construction, so nothing is unsound — but the benchmark must include a forked/overlaid graph with a non-trivial tombstone set, a high-cardinality seed predicate, and **peak RSS + allocation counts**, not only latency. Recommended repair before admission: decline when `rows.len()` or `Σ m_i` exceeds a multiple of `row_budget`/an absolute cap, or reuse the scan without copying subjects.

## F2 (measurement-gating) — decline paths that stack on the full fallback

`max_group = (n/2).max(256).max(2·row_budget)` and `failure_budget = max_group` mean a `LIMIT 1` query can probe up to ~n/2 candidates and then return `Ok(None)`. Counterexample cost shape: n=1000, k=1 → blocks 16/64/256, then `end-visited_to = 744 > 500` declines after 256 probes. The measurement must include the adversarial cases (skip-prefix just under the upfront-selectivity threshold; tie-group just over `max_group`) and report them, otherwise the reported gain is selection-biased. No performance claim is derivable from this source.

## F3 — tie order diverges across paths for the *same* query

`order_bindings(..., Some(row_budget))` tie-breaks on the collected-vector index. Selections are self-consistent across windows *while the indexed path fires* (collected is always a prefix in scan order), but a query paging past `TOP_K_ORDER_BY_THRESHOLD`, or losing admission after a write (overlay changes cardinalities → `min_other_card` check flips), switches to the fallback's own index order. Counterexample: 32 rows all `ak:priority 7`; `OFFSET 0 LIMIT 5` (indexed) and `OFFSET 5000 LIMIT 5` / post-write repeat (fallback) may return overlapping or omitted members. SPARQL permits it, `exact_desc_ties_…` asserts only membership, and no stability was claimed — but this is a user-visible pagination change and should be documented at the API level, not only in a private doc comment.

## F4 — no execution trace; engagement assertion is fragile

The fast path emits no `exec::trace` node, so `EXPLAIN ANALYZE` shows a plan with no operator for the work performed. `fast_path_actually_engages_not_just_correct` infers engagement from the *absence* of the literal `"BGP [binary GOO]"`; any label change, or a future path that also skips that evaluator, silently vacates it (and the `armed_*`/`multivalued`/`negative_*` fallback assertions with it). Emit an explicit trace/counter and assert on it.

## F5 — test-suite pinning gap

`indexed_path_disabled` kills exactly 1/26, which is expected but confirms nothing in the tie, offset-window, GRAPH-view, or fork/compaction tests pins *which* path produced the answer. Add the engagement assertion (F4) to `total_order_desc_offset_windows_match_full_sort`, `exact_desc_ties_…`, `forked_overlay_and_compaction_…`, and the `StoreDefault` leg of the view test; otherwise a future admission regression turns those into fallback-only tests without failing. Also uncovered: `match_count != 1` on an `obj_const` probe, and `Reduced` wrapping.

## Source needed (non-blocking, would sharpen F3/coverage)

`term_pattern_to_term` + `tp_var` for `TermPattern::Triple` (to confirm a quoted-triple object on a probe pattern is equivalent between paths rather than silently existence-only); `TOP_K_ORDER_BY_THRESHOLD`'s value (bounds admission and tells whether `randomized_sweep`/`crosses_block_escalation_boundary` k-values above it silently fell back); `eval_graph_pattern`'s modifier dispatch (confirms the GRAPH-nested `Slice{OrderBy}` test truly reaches this code).

Remaining obligations unchanged: full workspace build/clippy/nextest, feature-matrix legs, W3C conformance, wasm/`compact-index`/`zk` builds, and the bounded benchmark with the F1/F2 configurations before any performance claim.
